jsx-element.comment: One JSX element, opening tag through its matching closing tag (backreference \2) or self-close. Nested elements recurse through this same rule, so a self-closing child's own `/>` is consumed by the child's own end pattern before the parent's end is ever tested. `begin` is deliberately narrowed (issue #14 review, SHOULD-LAND-9) beyond a bare `<Name`: a lookbehind rejects a `<` immediately preceded by a word character, `>`, `)`, `]`, `:` or `.` (Rust generics/turbofish/qualified paths: `Vec<T>`, `impl<T>`, `x.collect::<Vec<_>>()`, `fn f<T: Clone>`), and a lookahead rejects a name immediately followed by only whitespace then `{` (`if a <b {}`'s own shape — indistinguishable from JSX's own rare spread-attribute form `<div {...x}>`, not supported by this grammar). This is a heuristic, not a parser: pathological Rust `<`/`>` usage can still be misclassified either way (`docs/grammar.md`'s real grammar resolves this with full tokenization, which a TextMate grammar cannot do) — see `packages/vscode-outou/README.md`'s own limitations section.
jsx-element.name: meta.tag.outou-rsx

jsx-tag-close-punctuation.comment: The opening tag's own unescaped `>` (transition from attributes to children). Self-close `/>` and the matching closing tag are handled by #jsx-element's own `end`, never here.
jsx-tag-close-punctuation.name: punctuation.definition.tag.end.outou-rsx

jsx-bare-attribute-name.comment: A valueless attribute (`<input disabled />`). Imprecise by construction (issue #14 review, SHOULD-LAND-9): this grammar scans an element's attributes and its children through the same `patterns` list (`#jsx-element`'s own patterns, not a separate opening-tag sub-scope), so a bare word here and an ordinary word of JSX text are the same shape to a regex with no parser behind it — a plain child-text word can be highlighted as a bare attribute name. See `packages/vscode-outou/README.md`'s limitations section.
jsx-bare-attribute-name.name: entity.other.attribute-name.outou-rsx

jsx-children-island.comment: A `{ … }` island among an element's children, re-entering Rust (grammar §6). Distinguished from an attribute-value island only by not being preceded by `=`; #jsx-attribute-expression-value is tried first and consumes the `=` case.
jsx-children-island.name: meta.embedded.expression.outou-rsx

jsx-island-body.comment: Content of a `{ … }` island: Rust that may itself contain nested JSX elements.
